content.text: {"per_criterion": {"heroes": "A", "craft": "A", "facts": "TIE", "age_fit": "A", "continuity": "A", "delight": "A"}, "verdict": "A", "confidence": 0.95, "justification": "These two stories are nearly identical, but Story B has a serious flaw: after the first chapter, Phoenix almost completely disappears. His name is swapped for Cruz's again and again, which creates impossible lines like \"Cruz grabbed Cruz's hand\" and \"Cruz carried planks. Cruz handed out nails.\" Cruz even suggests both company names in a row, and later answers his own line (\"'And kids who tested it all,' said Cruz\" right after Cruz has just spoken). Phoenix is only named again in the closing goodnight. In Chapter 8, two different speakers are also run together into one paragraph, so it sounds as if Cruz says Godtfred's line. A parent reading Story B aloud would stumble and have to fix it on the fly. One of their two children would also be left out of the adventure. In Story A, both boys share the action throughout. Phoenix gets the big test moment in the discovery chapter: he presses the tubed bricks together and shakes them upside down. That same chapter also gives Cruz his tube idea. Story A also reads cleanly from start to finish. The facts, the length, the gentle fire scene and the warm \"Play well\" ending are the same in both stories. So the whole difference comes down to the name mix-ups, and they make Story A clearly the better story to read at bedtime."}
